description:
FILED s473t4 (#1501 CHECK 1 round 1, 2026-09-13), found by FIXING the file that hid it: t/op/stat.t produced ZERO rows because `is_linux_container` was missing from the test.pl stub.  With the helper (shipped this session) it runs 44 rows and then ABORTS at

    ; PCL recovery: top-level form aborted (recovered):
        Error opening #P"/dev/tty": No such device or address

MINIMAL REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):
    for my $f ('/nonexistent/zz', '/etc', '/dev/tty', '/proc/1/mem') {
        my $ok = open(my $fh, '<', $f);
        printf "%-16s open=%-3s err=%s\n", $f, ($ok ? "yes" : "no"), ($ok ? "" : "$!");
        close $fh if $ok;
    }
    print "survived\n";

    perl:
      /nonexistent/zz  open=no  err=No such file or directory
      /etc             open=yes err=
      /dev/tty         open=no  err=No such device or address
      /proc/1/mem      open=no  err=Permission denied
      survived
    pcl:
      Unhandled sb-int:simple-file-error ... Error opening #P"/dev/tty": No such device or address
      (the program dies; the first two lines are not even printed because the
       whole top-level form is one statement list)

So PCL's `open` handles the errno classes it was written for and lets SBCL's
`simple-file-error` escape for the rest.  `/dev/tty` with no controlling
terminal (ENXIO) is the one this session met; `/proc/1/mem` (EACCES on a file
that EXISTS) should be checked in the same pass, and so should EISDIR, ELOOP,
ENAMETOOLONG and ETXTBSY.

PERL'S CONTRACT is absolute: `open` NEVER dies.  It returns false and sets `$!`.
So the fix is not "add ENXIO": it is that the open path catches
`sb-int:simple-file-error` (and `file-error` generally), maps the condition to
an errno for `$!`, and returns false â a rule-12 shape where the missing case
is a VALUE the program consumes, so it must not be silent OR fatal.

BEHIND IT: t/op/stat.t's remaining 67-row shortfall (the file reaches 44 of
perl's 111 rows).  Almost certainly other files too â the census should grep the
`sig` column for `Error opening` once this is fixed.
subject: A failing `open` whose errno SBCL raises (ENXIO on /dev/tty) KILLS the program -- perl returns false and sets $!; op/stat.t stops there
